cues: Most adverbs of manner add l y, but watch the false friends.
Hard means with effort; hardly means almost not: he works hard is praise, he hardly works is not.
Late and lately: lately means recently.
High and highly: highly means very much.
Near and nearly: nearly means almost.
Adjectives ending in l y, friendly, lovely, lonely, likely, are never adverbs, so say: he spoke in a friendly way.
And fast, hard and early have no l y form at all: never fastly.
